title: Optimizing Diversity and Quality through Base-Aligned Model Collaboration
claim: Single models trade diversity for quality; dynamically routing between a base and an aligned model reaches a better frontier with easy control.
layout: 2 panels: token-level example left, diversity-quality Pareto sketch right, color-coded by model
description: Panel A is a worked example for the prompt 'Suggest a summer trip destination in the US.' Aligned output (pink) is shown as one confident phrase with 90% probability, followed by a list of destinations led by Maui, Hawaii at 70%. Base output (orange) is shown with a 20% phrase and a more even list of destinations. Below them is a line plot of uncertainty per token against a dashed threshold γ. Points below the line route to the aligned model and points above it route to the base. The BACo output (blue) mixes both and yields a flatter list of destinations. Panel B is a Diversity vs. Quality plot. The orange base curve and the pink aligned curve each drop off as temperature changes. A blue dashed BACo curve sits above both and approaches a grey 'Desirable diversity-quality trade-off' arrow. Grey arrows connect the two panels. Color encodes the model throughout: orange for base, pink for aligned, blue for BACo.
caption: BACO is an inference-time token-level model collaboration framework that combines a base model’s diversity with its aligned counterpart’s quality. (A) A comparison of generated outputs. The aligned model produces high-quality but low-diversity outputs, while the base model produces high-diversity but low-quality outputs. BACO optimizes both diversity and quality by dynamically routing between them. The probabilities of token(s) are in grey next to text boxes. (B) Illustration of the diversity-quality trade-off space. Single models face a steep trade-off, where improving diversity by adjusting configuration (e.g., by increasing temperature) degrades quality. BACO achieves a better Pareto curve and allows for easy traversal across this frontier by adjusting the router’s threshold.
abstract: Alignment has greatly improved large language models (LLMs)' output quality at the cost of diversity, yielding highly similar outputs across generations, especially in open-ended generation tasks. We propose Base-Aligned Model Collaboration (BACo), an inference-time token-level model collaboration framework that dynamically combines a base LLM with its aligned counterpart to optimize diversity and quality. Using uncertainty and content-based signals, BACo employs routing strategies to determine, at each token, which model to decode from. Prior diversity-promoting methods often improve diversity at the expense of quality or require expensive decoding or post-training. In contrast, BACo achieves both high diversity and quality post hoc within a single pass, while offering strong controllability. We introduce a family of effective routing strategies and evaluate them across three open-ended generation tasks with 13 diversity and quality metrics. BACo consistently surpasses state-of-the-art inference-time baselines. With our best router, BACo achieves a 21.3% joint improvement in diversity and quality, which is further supported by human evaluations. Overall, our results demonstrate that collaboration between base and aligned models provides an effective and controllable mechanism for optimizing the diversity-quality trade-off.
